content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler Carrots, Stage 1 are gently cooked carrot pieces designed for children aged 6 to 12 months. The product is heat‑treated to provide a soft, safe texture while retaining most of the vegetable’s vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots are one of the first vegetables introduced to infants because of their mild flavor and easy digestibility.
Beta‑carotene in carrots is converted in the body to vitamin A, essential for vision and immunity.
Carrots are grown in over 100 countries, with China, the USA, and Russia being the largest producers.
Dried carrot sticks can be stored for up to 12 months under proper conditions, but freshly prepared pieces are best used within 3–5 days.
Carrots contain antioxidants such as lutein and zeaxanthin that support eye health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, cell growth, and immune function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C helps strengthen immunity and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids regular digestion and promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low allergen risk
items.content: Carrots rarely cause allergic reactions, making them a safe choice for most infants.

items.title: Supports bone development
items.content: Potassium and small amounts of calcium contribute to healthy bone growth.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Large carrot pieces can pose a choking risk for children under 12 months; serve as small, soft morsels.

items.title: Nutrient loss with over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive heat can reduce vitamin C content.

items.title: Potential contaminants
items.content: Ensure the product passes quality checks and is free from pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the carrots as tiny soft pieces, optionally mixed with apple or banana puree. A splash of breast milk or formula can be added for a smoother texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the package refrigerated at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, use within 3‑5 days. When frozen, the product retains quality for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Gordita is a Mexican flatbread made from corn masa that contains only cheese. The dough is prepared from corn flour, water and salt, then a generous amount of grated cheese is placed in the center and the flatbread is fried on a dry skillet until golden. The result is an aromatic, slightly crunchy snack with a rich buttery flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gorditas are traditionally served as a snack or side dish with Mexican foods such as beans or salsa.
Cheeses commonly used include cheddar, mozzarella or Mexican "queso fresco," giving each version a distinct taste.
The corn‑based dough makes the product gluten‑free, suitable for people with celiac disease.
The original recipe is cooked on a stone griddle (comal), but a regular skillet works fine at home.
Gorditas are often made in bite‑size portions, making them easy to eat with your hands.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The cheese provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cheese supplies high‑quality animal protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 in cheese is important for nervous system function and blood formation.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: The small amount of corn masa keeps the carbohydrate content modest, fitting low‑carb diets.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Certain cheeses contain live cultures that can benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese may cause discomfort for people who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy should avoid this product.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty, so those monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Both cheese and corn masa make the snack relatively calorie‑dense; moderation is key for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the gordita hot, straight from the skillet, as a standalone snack or paired with salsa, guacamole, beans, or fresh vegetables. Cut into bite‑size pieces for party platters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked gorditas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a dry skillet or oven to restore crispness before serving.

hot-dog-sandwich-reduced-fat-on-white-bu.title: Hot dog sandwich, reduced fat, on white bun

content.title: About
content.content: The reduced‑fat hot dog sandwich is a classic hot dog made with lean cooked or baked sausage meat placed in a soft white bun. Fat reduction is achieved by using low‑fat meat and limiting added oil during preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lower fat content makes this version more suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.
White buns usually contain less fiber than whole‑grain buns but are favored for their soft texture, especially by children.
The traditional American hot dog appeared in the early 1920s.
Lean chicken or turkey sausages are often used instead of beef to cut fat.
The sandwich is portable and popular at food trucks and sporting events.

items.title: Reduced fat
items.content: Less fat lowers the overall calorie count, which can help with weight management.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Lean sausage provides a good source of complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat supplies heme iron, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product contains B12 and B6, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Reduced fat makes the sandwich easier on the stomach, especially for those with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Meat or gluten allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to sausage ingredients or to wheat in the bun.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain high levels of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Low fiber
items.content: White buns provide little dietary fiber, so pairing with vegetables or whole‑grain sides is advisable.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Certain ready‑made sausages may contain nitrites and other preservatives that should be limited.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hot dog warm with mustard, ketchup, fresh vegetables (tomato, cucumber, lettuce) or a light yogurt‑based sauce. For a more balanced meal, add a side of fresh veggies or a whole‑grain accompaniment.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich refrigerated at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. Store sausages and buns separately to prevent moisture transfer. Sausages freeze well for up to 3 months; buns retain quality for about 1 month.

content.title: About
content.content: Mortadella is a cooked Italian sausage made from finely ground pork, sometimes blended with beef, pistachios, olives, mustard, and aromatic spices. It has a delicate, slightly spicy flavor and a characteristic pink color, often achieved with paprika or nitrites.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional mortadella originates from Bologna, where it is known as “mortadella di Bologna”.
The original recipe used only pork meat and fat, flavored with white pepper and nutmeg.
Mortadella is commonly served thinly sliced as an appetizer and used in sandwiches and salads.
In Italy mortadella is protected by a Protected Geographical Indication (PGI), guaranteeing specific production standards.
In some countries mortadella is mistakenly called “boudin” or “sausage”, though the products differ.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Mortadella provides about 15 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron in mortadella helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B12 and B6 contribute to energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports thyroid health.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Mortadella often contains 1.5–2 g of salt per 100 g, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Nitrites and preservatives
items.content: Nitrites are sometimes added to preserve the pink color; excessive intake is discouraged.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Fat can reach up to 30 % of the product, contributing to higher calorie intake.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to pork or sensitive to certain spices should exercise caution.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mortadella is usually sliced thin and served cold as an appetizer, added to sandwiches, salads, pasta dishes, or incorporated into hot recipes such as casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store mortadella in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it is best consumed within 5–7 days. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Vanilla cream pie is a dessert consisting of a tender crust filled with a fragrant vanilla custard. The crust is usually made from flour, butter, eggs and sugar, while the custard is prepared from milk, eggs, sugar and natural vanilla. The pie is served chilled or slightly warm, often topped with whipped cream or fresh berries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vanilla custard became popular in European cuisine in the 19th century as a lighter alternative to heavy pastry creams.
Traditional recipes use only natural vanilla beans, not artificial flavorings.
The pie is a common centerpiece for celebrations such as birthdays, New Year’s, and Easter.
In some regions, chopped nuts or dried fruits are added to the crust for extra texture and flavor.
The vanilla aroma intensifies when the pie is refrigerated for 12–24 hours before serving.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Both the crust and the custard contain eggs, providing a good amount of complete protein.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Dairy in the custard supplies calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Natural antioxidants
items.content: Vanilla beans contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The sugar and flour deliver quick‑acting carbohydrates for rapid energy replenishment.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: The scent of vanilla is known for its calming and mood‑lifting properties.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The custard contains milk and cream, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: A large amount of sugar makes the pie calorie‑dense and may raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The crust is typically made from wheat flour, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Butter and cream increase saturated fat levels, which should be considered in low‑fat diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve vanilla cream pie in slices, usually alongside tea or coffee. Garnish with fresh berries, mint leaves, or a dusting of powdered sugar. Store leftovers in the refrigerator and consume within 2–3 days.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the pie in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. For longer storage, individual portions can be frozen in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Allow frozen slices to thaw at room temperature for about 30 minutes before serving.

pork-potatoes-and-vegetables-excluding-c.title: Pork with potatoes and vegetables without carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens, no sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of tender pork, boiled or roasted potatoes, and a mix of vegetables that excludes carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens. It is prepared without sauce, allowing the natural juiciness of the meat and the flavors of the vegetables to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide and is rich in protein.
Potatoes are a primary source of carbohydrates in many diets and provide vitamin C and potassium.
Vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, and tomatoes add bright color and antioxidants to the dish.
The absence of sauce makes the meal easier to control for calorie content.
Traditionally the dish is cooked on a skillet or in the oven, preserving most nutrients.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Pork supplies complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑providing carbs
items.content: Potatoes deliver complex carbohydrates that release energy slowly.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables contribute vitamin C, vitamin A, and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Without sauce, the dish contains minimal added sugars, beneficial for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables and potatoes promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Pork can contain saturated fats; choosing lean cuts and moderate portions is advisable.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or intolerance to pork.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: If salt is added, monitor the amount to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Dryness without sauce
items.content: The dish may become dry if proper cooking techniques and ratios are not used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, slicing the pork into strips, cutting potatoes into wedges or cubes, and cutting vegetables into bite‑size pieces. Fresh herbs such as parsley or dill can be sprinkled for extra aroma. It can be enjoyed on its own or alongside a light whole‑grain bread side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers to room temperature, then place them in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.

potato-roasted-from-fresh-peel-not-eaten.title: Potato, roasted, from fresh, peel not eaten, made with margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Roasted potato from fresh product – sliced or wedged potatoes fried in margarine until golden. The peel is usually removed before cooking, giving a softer texture. This product is commonly used as a side dish or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Roasted potatoes are one of the most popular side dishes worldwide.
Margarine is used instead of butter to reduce saturated fat content.
The potato peel holds most of the fiber and vitamins, but it is often removed for a uniform texture when frying.
Potatoes contain about 77% water, which evaporates during frying, intensifying flavor.
Different countries serve roasted potatoes with various sauces, from ketchup to aioli.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potato flesh provides vitamin C, an important antioxidant.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates for energy
items.content: The complex carbs in potatoes deliver sustained energy.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: Potatoes contain plant protein that can complement the diet.

items.title: Fiber (when peel is kept)
items.content: Keeping the peel increases dietary fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Frying in margarine raises the calorie count, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some margarines may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Margarine allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to ingredients in margarine.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve roasted potatoes hot as a side to meat, fish, or as a standalone snack. Sprinkle with salt, spices, herbs, or accompany with sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked roasted potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in an oven to retain the crisp crust.
